name: xTool P3 80W
tagline: 2025 flagship 80W CO₂: ACS automation, huge bed, optional IR for metal
tldr: xTool P3 (August 2025) replaces the P2/P2S as the company's CO₂ flagship: 80W tube, 915×458 mm bed, integrated chiller, fire suppression, and ACS™ automation (cameras, LiDAR autofocus, AI nesting). Optional 5W IR module adds bare-metal marking. From ~$5,999: built for shops outgrowing diode lasers.
mainObjective: Automated 80W CO₂ production for sign shops and serious small businesses

priceRange.note: Standalone from ~$5,999; bundles with feeder, AutoLift, IR module extra

specs.dimensions: Large desktop footprint: plan dedicated space

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm acrylic

pros: Cuts clear and coloured acrylic, which no diode machine can do
Large 915 × 458 mm bed for full sheets and batch production
Integrated chiller and fire suppression replace kit a CO₂ setup normally needs separately
cons: Base unit around $6,999: a business purchase rather than a hobby one
Ducting to the outside is required for regular cutting
The glass tube is a consumable: budget its replacement over the years
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 80W SKU on xTool P3. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Plan exhaust before delivery. Run material tests on the full bed: large beds need focus calibration at corners. Price the IR module only if metal is a regular revenue line.

editorialDepth.advantages: xTool P3 is built for acrylic signage, thick wood, and shop production once exhaust is sorted. 80W adds headroom on panels and multi-pass jobs.
editorialDepth.limitations: Avoid without ducting, for occasional gifts only, or if budget ignores tube replacement, power, and floor space. Bare metal without an IR accessory stays out of scope.

moduleSystem.headline: Optional 5W infrared (1064 nm) module
moduleSystem.description: Base machine is 80W CO₂. Add the IR module for bare-metal and plastic marking without a separate fiber engraver.

faq.question: How thick can the xTool P3 cut?
faq.answer: xTool claims up to about 25 mm acrylic and 20 mm basswood, which at the top end usually means several passes. In our benchmark a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm acrylic took about 1–2 min, at 20–50 mm/s. Unlike a diode, the 80W CO₂ tube also cuts clear acrylic.

faq.question: How much does the xTool P3 cost?
faq.answer: The base unit listed at about $6,999 in the US in 2026 (retailers and Tom's Hardware's review). Bundles with the conveyor feeder, AutoLift and the IR module reach about $10,459. Budget extra for ducting to the outside and, over the years, a replacement tube.

faq.question: P3 alone or with the 5W IR module?
faq.answer: Take the P3 alone if your work is wood, acrylic, leather and coated metal. Add the IR module only if bare stainless or aluminium marking is recurring paid work: the CO₂ tube cannot mark bare metal, while the IR module does it on the same bed without a second machine, for roughly $1,299 to $1,899 depending on the bundle.

standoutFeatures.title: Cuts clear acrylic
standoutFeatures.body: The 80W CO₂ wavelength is absorbed by clear acrylic, so the P3 cuts transparent sheet with polished edges, a job diode lasers cannot do.

standoutFeatures.title: Chiller and fire suppression built in
standoutFeatures.body: The cooling and fire suppression are part of the machine, so there is no separate water chiller to buy and plumb.

standoutFeatures.title: 915 × 458 mm bed
standoutFeatures.body: The 36 × 18 in bed takes large sheets and batches of small parts in one job.
